    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}

vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

messages.content: The standard complement reduction applies: for the same graph on `n` vertices, a set is independent iff its complement is a vertex cover. So an independent set of size ≥ k exists iff a vertex cover of size ≤ n−k exists. I'll write `reduce.py` returning the same graph with `k` replaced by `n - k`, which handles all edge cases (k ≤ 0 → n−k ≥ n yes; k > n → n−k < 0 no).

function.arguments:
{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-9upv_8my && cat <<'EOF' > reduce.py
"""Polynomial-time reduction from Independent Set to Vertex Cover.

For a graph G on n vertices, a set S is independent in G if and only if
its complement V \\ S is a vertex cover of G.  Consequently G has an
independent set of size at least k exactly when G has a vertex cover of
size at most n - k.

The reduction therefore keeps the graph unchanged and maps the threshold
k to n - k.  It runs in O(len(edges)) time and never solves either
problem.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Map an Independent Set instance to a Vertex Cover instance.

    Input:  {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
    Output: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": n - k}
    """
    n = instance["n"]
    k = instance["k"]
    # Copy the edge list so the returned instance shares no mutable state
    # with the input (edges themselves are immutable pairs).
    edges = [list(edge) for edge in instance["edges"]]
    return {"n": n, "edges": edges, "k": n - k}
EOF

For a graph G on n vertices, a set S is independent in G if and only if
its complement V \\ S is a vertex cover of G.  Consequently G has an
independent set of size at least k exactly when G has a vertex cover of
size at most n - k.

k to n - k.  It runs in O(len(edges)) time and never solves either
problem.

def reduce(instance):
    """Map an Independent Set instance to a Vertex Cover instance.

    Output: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": n - k}
    """
    n = instance["n"]
    k = instance["k"]
    # Copy the edge list so the returned instance shares no mutable state
    # with the input (edges themselves are immutable pairs).
    edges = [list(edge) for edge in instance["edges"]]
    return {"n": n, "edges": edges, "k": n - k}
